title: Strategies to Cope With Larger Teams and More Direct Reports Than Ever Before
author: Admired Leadership
summary: The article takes on the organizational delayering trend, where reduced management ranks push individual leaders to oversee as many as 15-20 direct reports, and argues the resulting loss of coaching and oversight capacity is producing real damage: overwhelmed managers, disoriented teams, and problems that go unnoticed until they're unrecoverable. Rather than defending the trend, the piece treats it as a temporary crisis to be managed and offers concrete stopgap tactics — staggered biweekly one-on-ones, standing 'office hours,' peer buddy systems, and post-meeting overflow time for individual check-ins. It closes with a values statement rather than an efficiency argument: how leaders spend their time defines their leadership, and making time for people they lead remains the highest calling regardless of structural pressure.
points: The organizational delayering trend has pushed manager-to-report ratios as high as 15-20 direct reports, with reported overload and loss of team clarity as a direct consequence.
Reduced coaching capacity means problems catch leaders by surprise and are often beyond repair by the time they're noticed.
Practical stopgaps include staggered biweekly one-on-ones, standing 'office hours,' peer buddy/accountability systems, and short post-meeting overflow slots.
The piece frames making time for direct reports as leadership's 'highest calling,' independent of structural staffing pressure.
quotes: The ratio of managers to team members has increased dramatically in just a couple of years, with managers in many organizations asked to oversee as many as 15-20 direct reports.
With an ever-expanding number of direct reports, leaders no longer have the time to coach, guide, nurture, nudge, and mentor team members.
Because they are no longer on top of what team members are doing, problems that arise can catch leaders by surprise and are often beyond repair.
Instituting “office hours” where team members can rely on a set time to bring issues to the forefront and receive the guidance they need is another strategy worth considering.
How leaders spend their time defines their leadership. Making the time for those you lead is the highest calling and always will be.
